title: R-046 scalar tuning: budget-matched CMA-ES versus random search
hypothesis: CMA-ES can coordinate spin-drive and centering scalars to reduce destabilizing strokes, yielding more sustained successes than independent random draws at the same rollout budget.

prediction.against: Equal-budget random-search screen winners on identical fresh cases
prediction.rationale: A 10-percentage-point gain is four additional sustained successes per 40 fresh cases; compare independently selected screen winners across eight paired search blocks.

protocol.command: gpu run 'bash -lc "source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study r058_scalar_cma_vs_random --log-dir logs/pen_spin/r058_scalar_cma_vs_random"'
code_changes: New study module lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/scalar_tuning.py registered as --study r058_scalar_cma_vs_random in scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py; settings in the research_protocols block of config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml. No separate runner. The parent is config/pen_spin/r046_block3_incumbent (source and state hashes checked before any rollout); its source, gait, grasp pose, observation processing and action execution (clamp(mean, -1, 1)) are unchanged.

Scalar whitelist (12), bounds = the parent's own declared get_param_ranges, which contain both the frozen values and unsaturated operating points: spin: stroke_amp, lift_amp, spin_target, speed_gain, phase_lead, stance_sharpness; centering: center_gain, center_length, safe_radius, position_sharpness, tilt_gain, swing_damping. Search coordinates are bound-normalized to [0, 1]; every other parameter stays at its frozen value.

Eight independent blocks, seeds 4510-4517. Each seed freezes one 80-case Stage-3 development manifest (cases 0-9 screen, 10-39 promotion, 40-79 fresh; role slices via cases.role_manifests) at config/manifests/pen_spin_stage3_r058_block_s<seed>.yaml, placement-disjoint across blocks; hashes recorded before execution. Both arms and the parent share cases within a block.

CMA-ES arm: pycma (version recorded) with x0 = parent, sigma0 0.2 in normalized coordinates, bounds [0, 1] under pycma's own boundary handling, popsize 8, seeded per block; eight generations = 64 candidates. Fitness passed to tell is the frozen lexicographic screen rank (sustained successes first, fewer drops second, tail-hit fraction third, candidate index last), since CMA-ES uses ranks only. Random arm: a frozen copy of the same initial sampling law: for each of its eight generations a fresh pycma instance with identical options and boundary handling under its own deterministic seed derived from the block seed is asked once and never told; 64 independent candidates, no outcome-dependent update. The sampler options are recorded before any rollout.

Matched screening batches: every generation of either arm runs in one fresh Isaac process holding 8 candidates x 10 screen cases = 80 environments (candidate-major), so both arms see the same batch shape (D-035, D-037). Invalid or duplicate candidates are charged against their slots with no replacement, early stopping or extra probes. Each arm's screen winner is frozen (written to disk with its parameters and screen rank) before any promotion or fresh episode runs.

Per block: the CMA-ES winner, the random-search winner and the unchanged parent are each scored in their own process on the 30 promotion cases and in their own process on the 40 fresh cases, observations and actions recorded. Strict paired promotion rule against the parent on promotion cases (positive success difference and paired t-interval lower bound above zero; ties never promote). Fresh cases are confirmation only: they never select parameters, rerank candidates or trigger another search.
Per-block accounting: 2 x 64 x 10 candidate-screen + 10 parent-screen + 3 x 30 promotion + 3 x 40 fresh = 1500 episodes; 12,000 over eight blocks; zero LLM calls. About 23 Isaac processes per block.

Reporting: sustained success and drops for all three controllers, pooled and per block; drive saturation (fraction of recorded in-play steps with the parent's drive law 0.25 + 0.75 tanh(speed_gain (spin_target - spin)) above 0.99, evaluated from the recorded observations with each controller's own parameters) and executed-action saturation (fraction of executed components with |a| >= 0.99, overall and by axis), both over recorded in-play steps only (the runner records nothing after a drop, so no post-drop steps exist). Primary: paired 95% t interval over the eight block-level fresh CMA-ES-minus-random success differences. Secondary: each winner minus parent, paired success and drop differences with intervals, promotion and fresh. Intervals containing zero establish nothing.

Decision artifact (logs/pen_spin/r058_scalar_cma_vs_random/decision.json) for the deferred follow-ups R-056 and R-057, executed by neither: a repair parent requires strict promotion, fresh success with an interval lower bound above zero, and no observed increase in fresh drops; activated feedback (unsaturated drive fraction up by at least 0.25 with a positive paired interval) without a success gain routes priority to R-057 (R-043 re-scoped). Run only this protocol; no imitation, no cold search, no LLM call; the held-out split stays locked.

falsified_by: The upper bound of the paired 95% t interval for CMA-ES-minus-random fresh sustained success is below +0.10. Support requires a difference of at least +0.10 with an interval lower bound above zero; otherwise the result is inconclusive. Increased drops independently prevent adoption.

Reusing scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml, the 12,000-episode, zero-LLM-call protocol on free

direction: Resume Shadow Hand pen spinning from docs/SESSION_2026-10-27_PEN_SPIN_SUMMARY.md. First compare CMA-ES and random search at equal rollout budgets on the frozen R-046 controller's spin and centering parameters (config/pen_spin/r046_block3_incumbent). Compare both winners with the parent on fresh paired cases. Report sustained success, drops, and saturation. Keep final test locked. If tuning improves success without more drops, use the winner for repair. If feedback activates without improving success, prioritize R-043. Defer cold search and R-055. Require verified learner-state recovery before imitation. Use llm_pool with 16 workers and high reasoning effort. Run one protocol at a time.

advisor.reasoning: This directly implements the required first comparison using scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml, at 5,600 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls. It predicts paired_success_difference increasing by at least 0.10 for CMA-ES versus equal-budget random-search screen winners on identical fresh cases, refuted if the paired 95% interval upper bound is below +0.10. Equal candidate-rollout budgets, frozen screen selection, strict paired promotion, and eight independent blocks justify this spend; the weakest point is the four-generation CMA-ES horizon, so conclusions must remain budget-specific. Approve only this protocol, including parent comparisons and success, drop, and saturation reporting, with final test locked and neither conditional follow-up executed.

implementer.reasoning: The mechanism and the measurement are right and I want to run this first, but four edits are needed before the protocol is runnable and fair, so my position is revise, not approve. (1) Horizon: you name the four-generation CMA-ES horizon as the weakest point; at 4 generations of 6 the covariance has barely adapted, so a null result would say nothing about adaptive search. Each block is cheap (one Isaac process is about 20-30 s), so use 8 generations of 8 offspring = 64 candidates per arm per block (640 screen episodes per arm per block), which is still budget-specific but gives CMA-ES a real horizon. Per block: 2 x 640 + 10 + 90 + 120 = 1500 episodes; 12000 over eight blocks, about 2 h of wall time. (2) Random-search prior: drawing the random arm uniformly over the whole bounded domain confounds adaptive-versus-independent with local-versus-global. Draw the random arm's 64 candidates independently from CMA-ES's initial sampling distribution, N(parent, 0.2^2) in bound-normalized coordinates clipped to [0,1], so the arms differ only in adaptation. (3) Batch structure: a case's outcome depends on its batch (D-035, D-037), so both arms must evaluate candidates in the same batch shape: one fresh Isaac process per generation holding 8 candidates x 10 screen cases = 80 environments; the random arm is evaluated in 8 such processes of 8 candidates each, in draw order. Winners and the parent are then each scored in their own process on the 30 promotion cases and on the 40 fresh cases, as every pen-spin protocol does. (4) Interfaces: the script has --study and --log-dir, not --parent/--seeds/--output; the block seeds, parent hash, scalar whitelist, bounds and optimizer settings go in the config's research_protocols block. One frozen 80-case Stage-3 development manifest per block seed (cases 0-9 screen, 10-39 promotion, 40-79 fresh, role slices via cases.role_manifests), at config/manifests/pen_spin_stage3_r058_block_s<seed>.yaml; the three paths in the protocol do not match that convention. Whitelist (12 scalars, bounds = the parent's own declared get_param_ranges, which contain both the frozen values and unsaturated operating points): spin: stroke_amp, lift_amp, spin_target, speed_gain, phase_lead, stance_sharpness; centering: center_gain, center_length, safe_radius, position_sharpness, tilt_gain, swing_damping. Drive saturation and executed-action saturation are computed offline from the recorded observation and action traces of the three controllers' promotion and fresh runs (the runner records nothing after a drop, so pre/post-drop cannot be distinguished; this is stated as a limitation). CMA-ES is pycma (version recorded) with bounds [0,1], popsize 8, sigma0 0.2, seeded per block; fitness is the frozen lexicographic screen rank, since CMA-ES uses ranks only. Prediction, falsification rule and the strict promotion rule are unchanged.
changes_applied: 8 generations x 8 offspring per block (64 candidates per arm), 12000 episodes total
random arm sampled from CMA-ES's initial distribution N(parent, 0.2^2) in normalized coordinates, clipped, not uniform
both arms evaluated in fresh processes of 8 candidates x 10 screen cases

advisor.reasoning: This tests whether covariance adaptation coordinates spin and centering scalars better than independent local draws; I accept the implementer's longer horizon, matched batch shapes, corrected interfaces, and limitation to pre-drop diagnostics. The revised 12,000-episode, zero-LLM-call budget is justified using scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml, although conclusions remain specific to 64 candidates per arm. Retain the prediction that paired_success_difference increases by at least 0.10 for CMA-ES versus equal-budget random-search screen winners on fresh paired cases; falsified_by: the paired 95% t-interval upper bound is below +0.10. The remaining fairness gap is that clipping Gaussian random draws does not necessarily reproduce pycma's bounded initial sampling distribution, so the claim that the arms differ only in adaptation needs one correction.
suggested_changes: Generate the random arm's 64 independent candidates using a frozen copy of CMA-ES's initial sampling law, including identical boundary handling and any initial coordinate-scale adjustments, with independent deterministic RNG streams and no outcome-dependent updates. Freeze and record this sampler before rollouts; do not substitute clipped Gaussian draws unless CMA-ES uses exactly that same initial sampling procedure.

Consolidate the implementer's revisions into the canonical protocol: eight generations of eight candidates per arm, matched 80-environment screening batches, corrected --study r058_scalar_cma_vs_random and --log-dir interface, config-based settings, block manifests for free seeds 4510–4517, and a cost of 12,000 episodes and zero LLM calls. Preserve strict promotion, fresh-confirmation-only use, invalid-slot accounting, drop safeguards, and the locked final test; describe saturation as measured only over recorded in-play steps.

implementer.reasoning: Agree: revise, with your correction. The random arm will not use clipped Gaussian draws. It will be a frozen copy of CMA-ES's initial sampling law: for each of its eight generations a fresh pycma CMAEvolutionStrategy is constructed with exactly the options the CMA-ES arm uses (x0 = parent in bound-normalized coordinates, sigma0 0.2, bounds [0,1] with pycma's own boundary handling, popsize 8, any initial scale options identical) under its own deterministic seed derived from the block seed, and asked once; tell is never called, so no outcome-dependent update occurs. The sampler options are recorded in the config and in each block's summary before any rollout. I am applying the consolidated protocol as a revision patch now: eight generations of eight per arm, 80-environment matched screening batches, --study r058_scalar_cma_vs_random --log-dir, config-based settings, one 80-case block manifest per seed 4510-4517, 12,000 episodes, zero LLM calls, strict promotion, fresh cases for confirmation only, invalid-slot accounting, drop safeguards, saturation reported over recorded in-play steps only.
